English.Text: Divan Affairs — The Speech
At last the Divan of Wadi Al Zahir has granted me a seat among its members! Help me prepare my acceptance speech!
Thank you... for helping me understand what I needed to say in my speech.
I am not saying that, you scheming jackal!
The Envoy has been granted a seat in the city's Divan and wants your help preparing a speech.

Kemal Bey: 'I have several ideas on how to open my speech, but I cannot decide which would be most effective. First I shall rise and address them as "Honoured members of the Divan", then... Hm, what matters most in a first impression?'

Envoy Kemal Bey needs your help fine-tuning his acceptance speech for the Divan of Wadi Al Zahir. He has waited years for a seat on this council and does not wish to stumble at what he considers the final hurdle.
Kemal Bey: 'Good, I shall consider that... Now, the necessary flourishes and courtesies, and then on to the matter at hand: "There is much to be done. Our first mandate should be..."'
Kemal Bey: 'There will be much murmuring and debate at that point, I like to think— but I shall keep it well in hand. Now to the conclusion: "By the grace of Allah, I solemnly swear that..."'
'Your vote of confidence— for once in my life— humbles me...'
'I rejoice in joining forces with you for, clearly, the greater good of our city...'
'Long... very long... have I awaited this honour!'
'The needs of the humblest, as befits the virtuous...'
'To encourage piety and devotion at the mosque...'
'To lessen the burdens of the Envoys, that we may better uplift Wadi Al Zahir...'
'I will make my seat in the Divan my life's work!'
'I will not rest until the voice of this Divan is heard beyond Wadi Al Zahir, at the Sultan's very throne!'
'Order will be restored, and the righteous uplifted...'
The Envoy thanks you for the small part you played in composing his speech.
The Envoy does not offer even the faintest smile at your suggestion.
Help the Envoy compose his speech for the Divan
